questions.question: Which Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer was selected for the Asia Environmental Enforcement award by the United Nations Environment Programme in October 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramesh Pandey**__.

__
 
• Senior Indian Forest Service officer Ramesh Pandey was selected for the prestigious Asia Environmental Enforcement Award by the United Nations Environment Programme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **1996-batch IFS officer, posted as Chief Conservator Forests in Lucknow and Secretary**, UP State Bio-diversity Board, is known for his investigation and intelligence gathering on poachers.

 
 
• Pandey also received the award at the **United Nations Conference Centre in Bangkok.** 
 
• The purpose of the Asia Environmental Enforcement Awards is to publicly recognize outstanding achievements by public organizations and individuals in Asia to combat transboundary environmental crime.

questions.question: How many elements of India were listed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as of March 2018?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.**__

__
 
• 13 elements of India were listed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as of March 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• National List of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) of India:
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture** launched the National List of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) of India. 
 
• The National ICH List is an effort to recognize the diversity of Indian culture rooted in its intangible heritage.
 
• The initiative is also a part of the **Vision 2024 of the Ministry of Culture.**
 
 
 
• **UNESCO’s List of Intangible Cultural Heritage****:**
 
 
• **​**The list was established in 2008 when the Convention for Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage came into effect. 
 
• UNESCO maintains **three lists under its “Intangible Cultural Heritage”**:
 
 
• The list of intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.
 
• The list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity.
 
• The register of good safeguarding practices.

questions.question: In which of the following neighbouring countries of India is the famous Katas Raj Temple complex, with shrines of multiple faiths, located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The famous **Katas Raj Temples complex** is **located **in **Pakistan**.

 
 
• The** Katas Raj Temples** near Chakwal in the **Punjab province **of **Pakistan **are attributed to the **eras **of the **Hindu Shahis** (kings) dating from about 615-950 CE.
 
• This **splendid **complex of temples is **dedicated **to **Lord Ram**, **Lord ****Hanuman **and **Lord ****Shiva**.
 
• It is believed that the** site **was **visited **by the **Pandawa brothers **of "Mahabharta" fame and this complex of temples was **constructed **to **commemorate **t**heir visit**. 
 
• **Katas Raj **is **not just **a sacred **Hindu **site, though.
 
• A little distance from the pond is the remains of a **gurdwara **which Guru Nanak is believed to have stayed in during his journey around the world.
 
• There are also **shrines **associated with **different religions**.
 
• After **Partition**, while **ancient Buddhist **sites were preserved, and promoted, as part of the country’s rich history, the Hindu heritage was ignored as the trauma of Partition.
 
• In 1992, after the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya in India, many Hindu temples in Pakistan were destroyed.
 
• **Katas Raj **has a **collection **of **buildings **and **ruins **that **stretch **in an **unbroken line **from the **Buddhist era **down to **British rule**, thereby, **preserving **at least **1500 years **worth of **history **in that particular space.

questions.question: Which of the following is a famous fossil site in India where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waddham, Maharashtra.**__

__
 
• Wadham, Maharashtra is a famous fossil site in India where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Waddham** is a reserve forest and is a well-known fossils site where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found near the Godavari Basin in 1959.
 
• Paleolithic(stone age) tools were discovered in Wadham, Maharashtra.
 
• The well preserved **Barapasaurus skeleton** found at the site is at present kept in the **museum of Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Kolkata.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Manendragarh, Chhattisgarh is well known for a **sanctuary of marine fossils.**

 
 
• The Marine Gondwana Fossil Park is a unique appearance of **fossiliferous marine Permian rocks **of the Talchir formation recording back to around 280-240 million years ago. 
 
 
 
• Zanskar Valley of Kashmir is known for the world’s most diverse marine animals.
 
 
• The **trilobites at the Kurgiakh region of the Zanskar Valley** are from the beginning of the Cambrian age and are similar to those found in South China and parts of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• Hathnora of Madhya Pradesh is well known for** India’s earliest human fossils.**

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee of 2021, Kanaka Raju is associated with which of the following tribal folk dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Gussadi.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points:__

__
 
• **Kanaka Raju**

 
 
• He performs as an Indian gussadi dancer.
 
• He received the **Padma Shri honor from the Indian government in 2021 **for his contributions to the arts.
 
• Raju hails from the hamlet of Marlawai in the Komaram Bheem Asifabad district's Jainoor mandal.
 
• Gussadi dancing lessons have been taught by **Raju for more than 40 year**s.
 
• **In 1981, he again participated in the Republic Day procession**.
 
• As of right now, he serves as the Kanaka Raju School of Gussadi dance's chief dance master. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wancho** is a tribal folk dance form of the Wancho tribe in **Arunachal Pradesh, India.** 

 
 
• It is characterized by slow, graceful movements and is performed during festivals and social events.
 
 
 
• **Chalo **dance is performed by the **'Nocte tribe'** of Arunachal Pradesh to celebrate the auspicious festival of **'Chalo Loku'.**
 
• **Popir** is a traditional dance form of the Sherdukpen tribe in **Arunachal Pradesh, India.**
 
 
• It is performed during the Losar festival to celebrate the Tibetan New Year and involves intricate footwork and the use of traditional musical instruments.

questions.question: Which of the following is India's first all-women-managed railway station?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhinagar Railway Station, Jaipur.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's first all-women-managed railway station is **Gandhinagar Railway Station, Jaipur.**
 
• It is a historic step towards **women's empowerment** in the male-dominated railway industry.
 
• The station is managed by a team of **40 women**, including station master, ticket collectors, and security personnel.
 
• The initiative was launched by the **North Western Railway zone **in** 2017** to promote **gender equality and women's participation** in the workforce.
 
• The station has various facilities designed for the convenience of** women passengers**, such as a separate waiting room, washroom, and baby feeding room.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chennai Egmore Railway Station** is one of the **busiest railway stations** in South India.

 
 
• The South Indian Railway Company's terminus was constructed at the station between **1906 and 1908.**
 
 
 
• **Trivandrum Central Railway Station, Thiruvananthapuram **is the largest railway station in **Kerala.**
 
 
• It is the **busiest **train station in Kerala and a major Southern Railway rail hub.
 
 
 
• **Matunga Railway Station, Mumbai** is the first railway station in India to be entirely operated by women, but it is not an all-women-managed station.
 
 
• The station is managed by a team of **41 women, **but it also has male staff working in other departments.

questions.question: When was the Eden Gardens Stadium, Kolkata established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1864.**__

__
 
• **Designed in 1841, the stadium was established in 1864 and gets its name from the Eden Gardens, one of the oldest parks in Kolkata__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Eden Gardens is called the **“Mecca of Indian cricket”, **due to it being the first officially built ground for the game of cricket in India.
 
• The ground was named after the Eden sisters of Lord Auckland, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• Eden Gardens has hosted matches in major international competitions including the World Cup, World Twenty 20, and Asia Cup.
 
• It was established in the year 1864 and was laid by** Governor-General Auckland,** who named the gardens and the cricket ground after his sisters Emily and Fanny Eden.

questions.question: Which of the following is an open-pit copper mine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malanjkhand.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Malanjkhand** is an **open-pit copper mine** located in the **Balaghat district **of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• It is the **largest copper deposit** in India and one of the largest in the world.
 
• The mine is owned by **Hindustan Copper Limited,** a public sector undertaking under the **Ministry of Mines,** Government of India.
 
• The mining method used in Malanjkhand is an **open pit or surface mining,** which involves the removal of overlying rock and soil to access the copper ore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bastar** is a district in the Indian state of **Chhattisgarh,** which has significant reserves of** iron ore and limestone.** 
 
• There are **no copper mines** in Bastar.
 
• **Singhbhum** is a district in the Indian state of **Jharkhand,** which has significant reserves of **iron ore, coal, and copper.** 
 
• However, the copper mines in Singhbhum are **underground mines**, not open pit mines.
 
• **Ballari **is a district in the Indian state of **Karnataka,** which has significant reserves of **iron ore, manganese, and limestone.** 
 
• There are **no copper mines** in Ballari.
